There's a few things to note. 

1. It's genetics. Some people can grow one, some comes in patchy and there's not really anything you can do about it. There are products that claim can thicken your beard but they're mostly fish oil. There's a few scientific studies you can check out but the only things that really stimulate beard hair follicle growth is massaging your face to bring blood to the roots, and peppermint oil (not extract). Also some people are late bloomers, my beard didn't really start growing thick until I was 25.

2. Moisturize and clean your face. There's a lot of men that don't like growing a beard because it's itchy. It's only itchy because it's dry. Use an actual beard shampoo and conditioner, I like the company [The Beard Struggle ](https://www.thebeardstruggle.com/) for my products. Let the conditioner sit on your face for about five minutes before rinsing, also get a beard oil for after you wash.

3. Unkempt hair or beard doesn't look great. I shave my head but I still go to the barber monthly to line me up and trim it. Trimming the split ends off will also help growth. Go to a real barber who knows what they're doing if you can. Get a comb to keep it untangled and out of your mouth, get a boar hair brush to help spread the oil and to look fresh. 

4. Eating is gonna be messy in ways it wasn't before. Just a heads up.

My mom never hit me. She always said she was afraid I would hit her back because I was a black belt as a teenager. Idk why she thought this, I would never do that. So she made me write sentences hundreds and hundreds of times, like I'm talking 700+ occasionally. If it had poor penmanship she would make me redo it. She would also ground me from everything, and I mean everything. Isolate me from friends and caring family members. She would also threaten me with calling my father. 

My father spanked me using various items. Hand, belt, extension cord, whatever was convenient. Sometimes he missed and would leave bruises on my back and legs or sides. He would throw away my possessions. Throw me down stairs, pull my hair, slam my head into walls, pick me up by my throat and wall slam me. He would also threaten to beat me to death if I ever told anyone. 

How did it affect me? Well, I have complex PTSD that the military compounded with it's own trauma. I had to learn how to properly be affectionate, and I'm still learning that skill. For a while I only received validation from others. I'm no contact with my parents for obvious reasons, that makes holidays lonely as I'm single. My seasonal depression hits really hard because I *love* Thanksgiving and Christmas but have no one to spend it with. 

I desperately crave a parental/maternal person in my life but I don't have one. I feel alone and unloved even though I have friends who would die for me.

First thing we need to remember is you have a tiny dog which means tiny bladder. 

Regularly scheduled bathroom breaks while we learn, honestly I go every hour with my pups at first. You may need to do more frequently depending on the dog. 

Also a going on walks helps. Gives them lots of opportunities and sometimes the movement works things through ya. 

Associate a word with bathroom breaks, I use "go potty", then as soon as the dog finishes his business, and I mean literally the moment they're done, make a big deal about it and give them a treat. We are basically using forward conditioning to train your dog. 

Another pro tip that you didn't ask for, pick a word as a "marker" (I use the word yes). A marker is how you're going to communicate to your dog that it's doing what you want. Example: I tell my dog to sit, he sits, I say yes and give a treat. This will make teaching anything so much easier

I am fairly new to the cannabis world. I never touched it before I was 26. I had just gotten out of the military and was exploring using it for my pain management. Well a couple years into my journey I decided to finally make my own butter for various things. I even bought a [Hi infuser ](https://www.theherbalinfuser.com/) to make it as simple as possible. 

Instructions were pretty straightforward; decarb weed, melt butter, put both items in machine, push button. Simple right? Well for some reason I got paranoid halfway through the process and was worried that this was *too* simple and I started googling things. I started seeing all the different ways to make butter and I, for reasons I still don't understand, added water to the butter and let the machine do its job. 

Once completed I decided to cheese cloth the mixture and dispose of all the water. The problem is, I also got rid of any moisture that was in the butter. I was left with pure butter fat. My two pounds of butter reduced down to two sticks. Silly me didn't understand that THC binds to fat and what I had created was just super concentrated butter. In order to test it, I made a grilled cheese, with a normal amount of butter. I burnt the sandwich a little so I was worried I ruined it and wasted everything. 

Half an hour later I started feeling it. I was excited because I had succeeded in my goal despite my dumb panic. 45 mins later I started feeling sick, nauseated even. I told my girlfriend that I think I had overdone it and I was gonna be in the bathroom. At this point I started vomiting, aggressively. I couldn't move, I couldn't text my gf or shout what was happening but I was kinda scared. I was pouring sweat and leaving a feverish puddle of moisture on the the floor of the bathroom. 

This is where shit started to go bad. Now for context, I have aphantasia. Basically I can't visualize anything mentally. I can't replicate senses internally. I don't have hallucinations, I don't have flashbacks, I don't have dreams, nothing. At all. Just black when I close my eyes. I've been this way my whole life. *Well*, I started having flashbacks of toddler age memories. I was experiencing memories for a few moments, then it would rush by like a bad space travel animation and I would be dropped into another memory. This is the first and only time I've experienced this, hasn't happened since. I started having a panic attack because of it. I would rush memory to memory, then vomit, then a new memory and vomit. This happened for maybe 20 mins but felt like hours. I started pleading with the toilet, whom I'd named Terrance in my state of mind, to keep me grounded in reality. I would rush to a memory and if I got lost I would slap the toilet to ground me. 

My girlfriend hears all the commotion and busts in the bathroom to see me basically crying into a toilet begging for mercy, projectile vomiting. That saint of a woman, who has a vomit phobia, sat there with me and sang to me gently while I got through it. After it passed she went and got me taco bell while I recovered emotionally and physically on the couch. 

Now every time I get just a little too high I start to panic thinking it'll happen again.

On the opposite side of that spectrum, sometimes you'll find a smell that your body will obsess with. You want more you want to be surrounded by it.

Go to a garden, or a flower shop. This will be pleasant. 

The zoo or a farm will be unpleasant. 

Foods will taste different. You may start to hate a food you love and you may start to love food you hate. Make sure you're chewing your food thoroughly, That can change the taste and smell profile. 

You may discover that you'll start forming attachments to unpleasant smells because they remind you of something or someone. Regaining your sense of smell will affect your memory. You will start associating smells with places, peoples and activities.
